main_text.p: lum in diverfis Hominibus, quorum Ingenia & mores plurimum variantur; sed & in eodem, pro diversitate Ætatum atque studiorum. Quomodo igitur tam incerto Duci confidere possunt in Rebus Fidei, quæ non nisi Cælesti lumine discernuntur, & rite agnoscuntur, cum tam sæpe homines fallat, etiam in naturalibus & moralibus, quæ nobis multo propiora sunt, & intellectu faciliora? At certe multo iniquius & arrogantius est, sanam Rationem, præsertim in rebus Theologicis, sibi solis vindicare, quasi peculiarem quandam sectæ suæ Prærogativam; ac si alii omnes Christianismum profitentes sanæ mentis compotes haud essent. De Chinensibus quidem fertur, quod sua Genti soli binos oculos tribuant, Europæis unum, Cateris nentrum. At Sociniani, in hoc paulo arrogantiores, qui neque Europæis, paucis suæ sectæ exceptis, vel unicum concedunt. Illi Europæ incolas, non nisi luscos esse volunt; at Hi, plane Cæcos exifti-mant.

page.notes: The running head is partly unclear; "recta" is read from a worn word. The "pro" at the end of line 3 is followed by a small mark, but it is read as the whole word "pro" before "diversitate". Greek and Hebrew: none on the page. The text is a plain Latin transcription; the italic passage "sua Genti soli binos oculos tribuant, Europaeis unum, Cateris neutrum" is set in italic type as printed. Some letters in the final paragraph are read from a low-resolution scan, so "lusco" and "Cæcos" are uncertain readings and should be checked against the original.
